claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I've got one child - my son Alex, he's 9 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

**Are you responsible for Alex? That is, do you live with him and are you responsible for his day-to-day care (such as providing food, clothing, and ensuring he goes to school)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't actually live with me at the moment, but I do help support him. I send money regularly for his needs - you know, clothes, school things, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex doesn't live with you, but you provide financial support for him.

**Can you tell me who Alex currently lives with? For example, does he live with his other parent, another family member, or someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum - my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. 

**Does Alex's mum currently claim Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she doesn't claim it. That's why I'm looking into whether I can claim it myself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important situation to understand properly.

**Can you tell me why Alex's mum doesn't claim Child Benefit? For example, is it because she doesn't want to claim it, or is there another reason?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She just doesn't want to claim it - she's not interested in dealing with it, so I'm the one making sure he's provided for.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Just to clarify the living arrangements:

**Does Alex live with his mum full-time, or does he spend time living with you as well? For example, does he stay with you on certain days of the week or alternate weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he lives with his mum full-time. I don't have him staying with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: To claim Child Benefit, you must be responsible for the child, which means you need to **both live with the child and be responsible for their day-to-day care**. While I can see that you're providing financial support for Alex and making sure his needs are met, he lives full-time with his mother, not with you.

The key requirement is that you must live with the child. Since Alex lives with his mother and she has day-to-day responsibility for him (even though she's chosen not to claim Child Benefit), you don't meet the residency and responsibility requirements needed to make a claim.

I understand this may be disappointing given that you're supporting Alex financially and his mother isn't claiming the benefit. If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if Alex comes to live with you - you could then potentially become eligible to claim.

You do not live with Alex, which is a fundamental requirement for claiming Child Benefit. The person who has day-to-day responsibility for Alex and lives with him is his mother. Therefore, you do not meet the residency and responsibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex, even though his mother has chosen not to claim it herself.
